newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. council renews mandate of Prevlaka observers.
newsitem.headline: U.N. council renews mandate of Prevlaka observers.

text.p: The Security Council on Tuesday unanimously approved a six-month renewal, until July 15, of a 28-member U.N. military observer mission which monitors the demilitarization of the Prevlaka peninsula on the Adriatic coast.
Most of the peninsula, south of Dubrovnik, is controlled by Croatia but it borders Yugoslavia's republic of Montenegro and the main deep water port of its navy.
The U.N. Mission of Observers in Prevlaka (UNMOP) is commanded by Colonel Harold Mwakio Tangai of Kenya.

The council, in its resolution, called on the two sides to abide by their mutual commitments on demilitarization and to implement fully an August 1996 agreement on normalisation of relations between Croatia and Yugoslavia.
Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali, in a report before leaving office at the end of 1996, said Prevlaka remained stable but the potential for a military confrontation still existed.
The council called on the parties to adopt practical options proposed by the UNMOP last May for improving safety and security in the area.

It asked Secretary-General Kofi Annan to provide a progress report by April 15, particularly regarding freedom of movement for U.N. personnel throughout the entire area, where mines still pose a hazard, and respect for the demilitarization regime.
He was asked for a further report by July 5 on the situation in the Prevlaka peninsula as well as on progress by Croatia and Yugoslavia towards a peaceful settlement of their differences.
